chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from one of our companions, from one of the companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

Two men entered the Masjid; one was a worshipper and the other an immoral one. When they exited the Masjid, the immoral one became truthful (a siddiq) and the worshipper became immoral. This is because the worshipper entered the Masjid boasting about his worship, so his focus remained on that boasting, whereas the immoral one focused on remorse for his immorality and sought forgiveness from Allah, Exalted and Mighty, for the sins he had committed.

key_terms.صِدِّيقٌ: Truthful one / One of high spiritual rank

ai.seo_question: How does intention and self-conceit affect the spiritual status of a worshipper in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on the inner state (batin) over outward appearance, illustrating how pride (istikbar) in worship can degrade the righteous, while sincere repentance (tawbah) elevates the sinner. It underscores the scholarly principle that the quality of one's spiritual presence and humility determines true status more than mere ritual observance. This narrative serves as a caution against the subtle corruption of good deeds by self-conceit, a key theme in Shia ethical theology.
